newsitem.title: ITALY: POLL -Italy money mkt gloomier on near-term rates.
newsitem.headline: POLL -Italy money mkt gloomier on near-term rates.

text.p: The Bank of Italy's end-June cut in the discount rate has not brought about easier money market rates and operators' expectations are gloomier than in recent weeks, a study based on implicit forward rates showed.

The study by Bocconi University's Igier research arm showed the market expects to see rates still around seven percent in the next month while a drop below the six percent level is not likely for at least a year.

On a one-month horizon, the market saw the implicit overnight rate at 6.94 percent, up on expectations of 6.83 percent a week ago but below an actual close of 7.10 percent on Thursday, the day on which the study was based.
One a three-month timescale, the market saw the o/n rate at 6.67 percent against 6.57 percent seen a week ago and 6.74 percent one month ago.
A year out, the o/n rate is seen at 5.93 percent unchanged on last week's forecast while one month ago operators were more pessimistic and saw the rate at 6.47 percent.
Last week's Igier study was published on June 27. Later the same day the Bank of Italy announced a 50 basis cut in the discount rate taking it to 6.25 percent.
Two year's out the implicit o/n rate is seen at 5.72 percent from 5.90 percent a week ago.

The spread between the Italian and German implicit o/n rates, considered a good indicator of market confidence in Italy's entry into the single European currency, dropped to 132 basis points from 145 bps a week ago.
